zoe (People Ops): Quick Q for managers: when nominating for out-of-cycle promos, what's the minimum evidence you want? trying to keep submissions short.

carlos (Eng Manager): Prefer 2-3 concise examples, each with timeframe, direct impact, and validation link. Metrics if possible.

anya (IC): If impact is customer-facing (reported bug fixes that saved accounts), can we include customer emails as evidence?

zoe (People Ops): Yes, redacted customer notes are fine. One-line context + 1-2 sentence quote + link to ticket.

carlos (Eng Manager): Also include whether this is retention-driven vs role-evolution. Committee treats them differently.

anya (IC): What about people who are doing manager-like work but haven't changed title?

zoe (People Ops): We accept "acting" responsibilities as evidence. Manager should note scope, duration, and who supported/verified. If <3 months, mark as "emerging".

comp-bot: :rotating_light: Reminder: Out-of-cycle promo form: https://go.company/out-of-cycle-promo (deadline in 7 days)

carlos (Eng Manager): If comp bands are frozen, will we still get title promotions?

zoe (People Ops): Possible. Two tracks: title-only with documented path, or title+comp if budget allows. Include suggested timeline to comp band move.

anya (IC): For equity catch-ups, who signs off?

zoe (People Ops): Equity adjustments go to People Ops comp + recruiting. Attach current grant details and target.

carlos (Eng Manager): Last: what's the recommended way to reconcile mixed peer feedback?

zoe (People Ops): Add a short reconciliation note in your submission explaining differences and pointing to objective evidence. Committee leans on manager narrative + hard evidence.

anya (IC): Thanks, very helpful.

zoe (People Ops): I'll post a two-paragraph manager template and a short checklist in the promo toolkit by EOD. DM for urgent cases.
